faqs.q: How much will it cost to get wildlife out of my Madison home?
faqs.a: It depends on the job — a single squirrel entry sealed early is very different work from a raccoon family in a chimney or a bat colony in the attic. We inspect first and provide a straightforward quote after inspection, so you know the full scope before any work starts.

faqs.q: What should I do about a snake in my Madison basement?
faqs.a: Do not try to kill it — it is illegal to kill any snake in the wild in West Virginia, and most basement snakes here are harmless rat snakes hunting mice. Call us: a licensed WDCA identifies it, captures it non-lethally, and liberates it at the site of capture, then we find and seal the gap it used.

faqs.q: What should I expect to pay for wildlife removal in Danville?
faqs.a: Cost turns on the animal, where it has gotten in, and how much proofing the building needs afterward. Our crew walks the property, shows you the entry points, and gives you a quote after inspection before work begins.

faqs.q: Why do raccoons get into Danville chimneys every spring?
faqs.a: An uncapped chimney reads as a hollow tree to a raccoon mother, and the valley's older homes offer plenty. Our crew checks for pups first, removes the family together where we can, and fits a proper cap — a chimney left uncapped will be re-denned within a season or two.
